answer.exemplar: A ruler's reach has to survive his absence, and a command that travels on the loyalty of a single man dies with that man's service or with his master's favour, which sets a ceiling on any reputation. A schedule applied without local variation does the opposite of what personal rule does: it makes the same demand on every district, so a district is not administered well or badly according to who happens to be posted there. Periodic returns then close the loop, because the centre learns what has been collected and can correct the discrepancy while the quarter is still running, instead of learning of it afterwards. A strong answer names these as administrative rather than personal conditions, and is willing to say what they did not do, since the apparatus relays commands and revenue but does not by itself produce obedience.
